title: Steady Roll: multi-instrumentalist partner at Cairo
summary: Slim recalls working with Steady Roll around Cairo and Missouri, the poisoned-alcohol quarrel, and learning chords from him.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: And, you know, I just, I like Lonnie Johnson, his brother, Sturdy Roll. Sturdy Roll, yes. Sturdy Roll, yes. Yeah. Well, see me and Sturdy Roll used to, I, I jumped on a boy, he's police here now, about getting him some alcohol, made him sick so he, we couldn't make a Sunday evening party, which I wanted that three and a half, you know. And me and Sturdy Roll was getting the same dollars. That was a lot of money at that time.

And so, and, and, you know, but I was coming in and he made me mad. He told me he had some whiskey, Sturdy was really alcohol, like to drink whiskey. He burnt some alcohol and messed it up, that something, and gave it to him some water, coke or something, I don't know how to, made him sick and made him foam at the mouth. We got, we got, we got, I got Miss Vison to get a doctor there, 20, 30, and pop them. And she got him, we got him straight, but he didn't, he didn't come two times away, so. See, Sturdy was a diverse man. He played drum, played piano. He played fiddle or either guitar. Oh, yes. He wouldn't like Lonnie, he could play it all. Lonnie played a little piano, you know. And I don't know about the fiddle, but I know Sturdy played all of them. Drum, guitar, fiddle, a little violin, and the guitar played a good guitar. So, me and him just, well after we got together I had a little place, that 507 commercial after I got there, I got a little, good time girl there, and they'd all hang around me, you know, back like I got there, I got to go. I studied, he and him would get them little old jobs, and people would go for us playing, no style, the boogers would go, and he could play, he'd teach me a lot of chords, you know. Sturdy Rose? Yeah, he'd teach me a lot of chords. When and where? At Cairo. He had been to East St. Louis and St. Louis. Me and Sturdy stayed together about a year, a year ahead there. A future city, a mound, a mound, and a mound city, and, uh, well, Kaelin was in a bloom game. And we went over to a wide, Missouri, and we went to Saxton, Missouri, me and Sturdy were all heavy, and we'd get along fine. But I got mad at the Snoop, he's a policeman here now. Everybody's here. He do, he, he tried to get some quick money and give him some old alcohol, you know, just old alcohol out of a bottle, it's so lucky to rub your soul or face. And he doped it up and get set it all, made him sick, and made me mad, you know. We had a three and a half dollar job apiece. You were on the water walk? So, fact of business, we were together, uh, more than anyone that type. Now, the first man I supposed to start running with here was Sonny for us.
You've got to be a man.
